definitions.human_turn: one operator-typed prompt; synthetic user records (tool results, task notifications, interrupt markers, compaction continuations, slash-command echoes) excluded
definitions.slash_turn: prompt whose whole text is a single /command; counted, excluded from the altitude denominator
definitions.rendered_turn: Copilot user.message_rendered with no verbatim user.message; machine-composed brief, excluded from the altitude denominator by default
definitions.off_project_turn: >=2 off-domain markers and 0 markers of the folder project; non-engineering work done in a corpus folder
definitions.canonical_human_source: claude_history for Claude Code, user.message for Copilot; claude_code transcripts contribute assistant/token/tool volume and a cross-check only, never a second copy of the human turns
definitions.paste_chars: characters of pastedContents attached to a history prompt (the operator's clipboard payload, not typed)
definitions.attribution: folder | path (explicit foreign project path) | signature (>=2 foreign markers, 0 own) | alias (seam-reproduction -> seamQ)

btest.reason: First commit. Owns all SMIM work before 2026-05-02 and all EODHD tooling work before 2026-07-09, because those trees lived inside btest until they were extracted.

b-autobot.reason: Bootstrap prompt in history 2026-03-03; git span 2026-03-05..03-11; nothing after March. Bounded end stops later 'cucumber/maven' chatter from being read as b-autobot work.

blive.reason: First commit 2026-04-26 (the day claude.ai authored Requirements v0). End extended past the last commit (2026-06-06) because the method paper continued to live in blive/docs/method/paper into July.

smim.reason: Standalone repo created 2026-05-02 (single squashed commit). Before that date SMIM was src/quantdsl_backtest/smim inside btest, so its turns are btest's - this is what blocked four March/April false positives.

harp.reason: Repo created 2026-04-08 out of btest (the creation prompt itself was typed in the btest folder). Open end: the paper went to arXiv/SSRN in June, well after the last commit.

datacli.reason: Extracted from btest 2026-07-09 (btest commit 5e8cd8f). Raw EODHD snapshots stay in btest, so datacli sessions legitimately run in the btest folder.

seamQ.reason: claude.ai handoff/kickoff artifacts dated 2026-04-30 precede the first commit (2026-05-16) by over two weeks (OQ-2). The git span is not the project span.

cross_source_check.note: history.jsonl and the transcripts are parsed by different filters over different files; the deltas that remain are queued/edited prompts recorded once but delivered differently. history.jsonl is the canonical human-turn source; transcript turns are NOT added to it, so no Claude Code turn is counted twice.

_meta.hand_verification: Three independent hand-checks before the analysis passes. (1) Per-folder history.jsonl prompt counts reproduced exactly by 'grep -c' for all ten folders: btest 842, b-autobot 123, blive 119, seamQ 57 + seam-reproduction 30, shared-substrate 26, harp 11, datacli 6, smim 2, lab 2; sum 1218 = wc -l of the file. (2) Copilot session f83d6027: 'grep -o' counts 73 raw user.message events against the miner's 65 turns - the store re-emits a user.message on retry/edit, so dedup by turnId is required, not cosmetic. (3) Cross-source: 11 Claude Code sessions exist in BOTH history.jsonl and the transcripts; 9 human-turn counts match exactly and the two deltas are exactly 1 turn each, hand-explained (a014aa48 'close to 50 or 70' typed while a tool was running, recorded in history and absent from the transcript; 3cd3a1cd trailing 'exit'). Two real defects were caught by hand-reading rather than by the counts: four March/April turns were being re-attributed from btest to smim although SMIM was still a package INSIDE btest until 2026-05-02 (fixed by attribution windows), and an eight-turn printer-troubleshooting session in the btest folder was being counted as btest operator turns (fixed by session-level off-project pooling).
_meta.privacy_note: The published JSON carries a 160-character preview and a sha1 per turn. Verbatim prompt text is written to local, which is gitignored: re-running the script reproduces it from the local log stores.
